title: SCONE: A Logic Locking Technique Utilizing SMT Solver and Circuit Encoding Scheme for Efficient Hardware IP Protection
problem: Stripped-Functionality Logic Locking (SFLL) with Distance-2 Protected Input Patterns (D2PIPs) provides security but faces scalability challenges, lacks flexibility in key derivation, and shows vulnerabilities to advanced structural attacks.
motivation: Hardware IP security in complex IC supply chains requires robust, scalable logic locking techniques that resist both input-output and structural attacks while minimizing design overhead.
method: SCONE combines a Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solver with a novel secure circuit encoding scheme to generate protected input patterns. SMT enables scalable constraint satisfaction; the encoding scheme provides security against structural attacks while maintaining flexibility in key space design.
key_novelty: Integration of SMT solver with circuit encoding scheme achieves 350x scalability improvement while maintaining resilience against five categories of I/O and structural attacks.
contributions: SMT solver-based approach for scalable protected input pattern generation
350x scalability improvement on IBEX processor (16K gates)
Resilience against both I/O-based and structural attacks
primary_theme: SMT-based logic locking with secure circuit encoding for IP protection
